newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end mixed, bargain-hunting seen.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end mixed, bargain-hunting seen.

text.p: Singapore shares finished on a mixed note Tuesday with the index lifted by bargain-hunting while the over-the-counter (OTC) issues sagged, dealers said.
Institutions bought selected large capitalisation stocks but volumes remained relatively thin.
"There was late bargain-hunting from both sides of the causeway and probably some recommendation notes might have come out," a remisier said, noting good liquidity in some counters.
The Straits Times Industrials Index closed up 9.67 points at 2,047.56 on a moderate turnover of 136.4 million shares.
The UOB OTC index, tracking mostly Malaysian stocks, fell 12.38 points to 1,176.87, confirming the still-fragile nature of speculative small-capitalisation issues, dealers said.

Leading gainers was SPH foreign which ended Singapore $1.20 (US$0.83) up at S$27.50. Electro Resources remained firm, rising S$0.22 to S$2.74 after it was upgraded to the mainboard. City Development also saw healthy volume spurred by recommendations. It ended S$0.30 up at S$12.80. Singapore Telecom fell S$0.08 to end at a new low at S$2.64 in active volume of 5.6 million shares. SingTel remained weak after the partial deregulation of Singapore's telecommunications market.
